(1) the theory transformation method presented in this paper is sound, i.e., it always produces terminating theories, (2) the theory transformation is complete, in the sense that, if the original theory is terminating, then the transformed theory is terminating, and (3) the prototype tool is correct, in the sense of preserving the semantics of the original theory

the transformation sequence we present can be used to prove termination of equational theories that are expressible using the aforementioned features, and that our prototype tool, <sc>Terminology</sc>, can automatically perform the transformation sequence and send the results to the termination tools.

we have found a way of proving termination of equational programming languages that have very general conditional rules (such as <sc>Maule</sc>) and have developed a prototype tool that can be used for proving the termination of such programs.

our method is a practical way to prove termination of <sc>Maudes</sc> and other equational programs having advanced features.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a given equational program in a given language with a given set of features, we can always find a sequence of theory-transformations that, when applied, will result in a theory with the same behavior as the original theory, but with a subset of the features of the language.

we have developed a new theory transformation method that is capable of handling the expressive features of <sc>Maudes</sc> equa- tional programs and is applicable to a large number of termination tools.
, for the first time, we can prove the termination of <sc>Maudes</sc> having advanced features and very general conditional rules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to use the expressive features of equational languages in a controlled way that preserves termination, and that this is possible without having to give up on using termination tools.
, with the help of our theory transformation tool, expressive equational programs can be analyzed by existing termination tools, thus providing a new way to analyze the termination of such programs.
it can be possible to prove termination of expressive equational programs using standard termination techniques.
